jobs.title: Slalom Flex - Wildfire Mitigation / PSPS Program Analyst (Multi-year Contract)
jobs.description:
Role Overview

Slalom is seeking a Wildfire Mitigation and PSPS Program Analyst to support a large Southern California utility's Emergency Management function. The utility is expanding its wildfire mitigation and Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) capabilities in response to increasing climate driven risk from rising temperatures, drought, and extreme weather.
Reporting into the utility's wildfire mitigation program leadership, this role provides the analytical, documentation, and coordination support that keeps the program running. You will help maintain and improve PSPS plans, protocols, and standard operating procedures, support situational awareness tools and reporting, and provide direct support to emergency operations personnel during activations. This is a hands-on execution role for someone who is strong on process documentation, data, and coordination in a high stakes operational environment.
This is a contract position with the opportunity to apply for a permanent role with the utility.

This position will require 3 days per week onsite to local LA office.
What You’ll Do

Support the ongoing operation of the utility's PSPS program, including maintaining operational workflows, tracking action items, and coordinating across teams to keep program activities on schedule.
Draft, update, and maintain plans, protocols, and standard operating procedures for wildfire mitigation and PSPS, ensuring alignment with Emergency Management practices, ICS and NIMS principles, safety requirements, and regulatory expectations.
Document PSPS event lifecycle processes across pre-event, during event, restoration, and after-action phases, and keep procedural documentation current as the program evolves.
Support situational awareness capabilities by compiling and quality checking weather data, fire risk indicators, asset information, and field status inputs, and helping maintain the dashboards and reports leadership relies on.
Prepare analysis, briefing materials, and status reporting that help leadership and emergency operations personnel make timely decisions during wildfire and PSPS conditions.
Participate in exercises, drills, and post incident reviews, capturing lessons learned and turning them into updates to plans, tools, and procedures.
Track evolving wildfire and climate risk practices across the utility industry and summarize relevant developments for the program team.
Support Department Emergency Operations Center activations with shift-based overtime or on call work, including nights, weekends, holidays, and extended hours.
This position's work mode is in person.

What You’ll Bring

3 or more years of experience in emergency management, business continuity, utility operations, wildfire mitigation, or a closely related field
An understanding of utility operations, with prior experience at an electric utility, municipal utility, or public power agency preferred.
Experience writing and maintaining plans, standard operating procedures, and operational documentation, with strong written communication skills.
Solid analytical skills, including comfort working with operational data in Excel and building or maintaining reports and dashboards.
Familiarity with ICS and NIMS and how organizations coordinate during incidents. ICS 100, 200, 700, and 800 completed, or willingness to complete them within the first 60 days.
Ability to organize work, track commitments across multiple stakeholders, and keep documentation current in a fast-moving environment.
Comfort operating in ambiguity and change, including responding to evolving risk conditions and time sensitive events.
Availability to support activations outside of standard business hours.

Nice to Have

Exposure to PSPS, de-energization, Wildfire Mitigation Plans, HFTD, or CPUC and Energy Safety reporting.
Emergency management credentials such as CEM or AEM, or experience supporting a local or state EOC.
Experience with SharePoint, Power BI, Tableau, or ArcGIS.

About Us
Slalom is a fiercely human business and technology consulting company that leads with outcomes to bring more value, in all ways, always. From strategy through delivery, our agile teams across 52 offices in 12 countries partner with clients to co-create powerful customer experiences, modern ways of working, and meaningful impact. 
What sets us apart? We believe work should be challenging and fulfilling, not perfect, but possible. That’s why we prioritize purpose, flexibility, connection, and recognition, so our people can thrive and love what they do, most days. 

Compensation and Benefits
Slalom prides itself on helping team members thrive in their work and life. As a result, Slalom is proud to invest in benefits that include meaningful time off and paid holidays, parental leave, 401(k) with a match, a range of choices for highly subsidized health, dental, & vision coverage, adoption and fertility assistance, and short/long-term disability. We also offer yearly $350 reimbursement account for any well-being-related expenses, as well as discounted home, auto, and pet insurance.

Slalom is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The targeted hourly pay range is $55/hr to $85/hr.   Actual compensation will depend upon an individual’s skills, experience, qualifications, location, and other relevant factors. The hourly pay range is subject to change and may be modified at any time.    

We are committed to pay transparency and compliance with applicable laws. If you have questions or concerns about the pay range or other compensation information in this posting, please contact us at:  peopleone@slalom.com . Please note, this recipient is not able to support recruitment inquiries beyond this purpose.

EEO and Accommodations
Slalom is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to attracting, developing and retaining highly qualified talent who empower our innovative teams through unique perspectives and experiences. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. Slalom will also consider qualified applications with criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. Slalom welcomes and encourages applications from individuals with disabilities. Reasonable accommodations are available for candidates during all aspects of the selection process. Please advise the talent acquisition team or contact  accomodationrequest@slalom.com  if you require accommodations during the interview process.

jobs.description:
På ABB
hjälper vi industrier att bli mer resurseffektiva och renare – och varje person här bidrar till resultaten. Du kommer att få möjlighet att leda, få stöd att växa och kunna vara stolt över den påverkan vi skapar tillsammans. Gå med oss och hjälp till att driva det som driver världen.

Denna Position Rapporterar Till

MOIM Chief Information Officer (CIO)

__

Your Role And Responsibilities

We are seeking an experienced IT/IS project manager to lead our Motion IEC Low-Voltage Motors division's global strategic initiatives, with particular focus on coordinating SAP Ariba SCC activities across the Motion Business Area. This role combines project management expertise with digital transformation responsibility, requiring the ability to self-organize and manage complex projects of varying sizes while acting as either an IS project manager or a combined Business/IS role. The successful candidate will lead end-to-end SAP Ariba solution implementations, drive cross-functional project teams, ensure seamless ERP integration, and continuously improve procurement and supply chain capabilities through training, best practice sharing, and alignment with ABB's business objectives, while working closely with the global MOIM IS PMO and P&F leadership.

If you are passionate about leading strategical Divisional IS projects and coordinating the future MOIM ARIBA SCC path and activities and have a proven track record for these topics, we would love to hear from you.

The work model for the role is: hybrid;

The role is contributing to the Motion / IEC LV Motors globally.

You Will Be Mainly Accountable For

Driving IT/IS projects and contributing to continuous improvement of MOIM IS project management maturity.
Leading full lifecycle SAP Ariba SCC implementations, including planning, blueprinting, configuration, testing, go-live, and post-deployment support.
Coordinating ARIBA training programs and best practice sharing to ensure continuous improvement and optimal utilization of SAP Ariba solutions.
Collaborating with business stakeholders, external implementation partners, vendors, and SAP support teams to translate procurement requirements into functional specifications and deliver successful implementations.

Qualifications For The Role

5-8 years of experience as an IS Project Manager role within a global matrix organization
Experience with SAP ARIBA SCC solution, as well as implementation, experience with Operative Procurement and Quality processes is a plus.
Proven experience leading complex and distributed projects.
Knowledge of MM module in SAP ERPs is an advantage.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, ability to influence and lead without direct authority.
Problem-solving ability, resourceful in identifying challenges and proposing tailored solutions to meet client expectations.
Self-organized, self-structured with solid strategic understanding.
Customer-centric approach, drive to understand the clients’ business and ability to prioritize their needs to deliver maximum value.
Fluent English language skills.

More About Us

The IEC Low Voltage Division is a technology leader delivering a full range of energy-efficient low voltage motors, including ultra-efficient solutions such as IE5 SynRM (synchronous reluctance motors). Through a global footprint, domain expertise and rugged designs, the Division provides reliable technology that improves efficiency and productivity even in the most demanding applications.

jobs.title: Technical Project Manager III – Data Analytic Solutions
jobs.description:
Hybrid role (3 days/week in office) at our Salt Lake City, Boise, Fargo, Portland, Vancouver, Renton, Medford, Burlington, Lewiston, Little Rock, and Springdale offices.

Preference will be given to current employees and candidates who reside within a commutable distance from our Salt Lake City, Boise, Fargo, Lewiston, Little Rock, and Springdale offices, or who are willing to relocate.

Build a career with purpose. Join our
Cause
to create a person-focused and economically sustainable health care system.

Who We Are Looking For

Every day, Cambia’s Technical Project Managers are living our mission to make health care easier and lives better. As a member of the Data Analytic Solutions team, the Technical Project Manager III manages work efforts from concept through close-out and supports the management of work efforts of varying complexity and technical scope. The Technical Project Manager III is responsible for the appropriateness, quality, and timeliness of all aspects of one or more work efforts, in coordination with an agile or PMO Project Manager where applicable, managing the production of work effort estimates, developing delivery plan and schedule, establishing measures and milestones, and tracking ongoing progress, while proactively managing risks, issues, scope and human resources through the delivery life-cycle.

This position handles the largest and most complex of assignments and may lead teams of people to ensure work efforts are delivered on schedule and within budget, while satisfying agreed-upon customer requirements and specifications within the scope of the work effort, and will generally have a certification and will work with or on an agile team.

Do you thrive as part of a collaborative, caring team? Then this role may be the perfect fit. 

Qualifications

What You Bring to Cambia:

The Technical Project Manager III
would have a Bachelor's Degree in Business or related field and a minimum seven years progressive project management experience to include managing multiple, large scale or highly complex projects concurrently, with a ScrumMaster Certification (CSM) or PMI-ACP certification (PMI Agile Certified Practitioner) preferred or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Required Licenses, Certifications, Registration, Etc.

ScrumMaster Certification (CSM) or PMI-ACP certification (PMI Agile Certified Practitioner) preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Large-company experience: Experience working in a larger, more complex organization, including navigating matrixed teams and established processes
Technical project management: Proven track record managing projects with technical components from planning through delivery
Internal and vendor collaboration: Experience partnering with cross-functional internal teams and managing external vendor relationships
Complex project delivery: Has led or contributed to projects with multiple workstreams, dependencies, and competing priorities
Stakeholder management: Skilled at communicating with, aligning, and influencing stakeholders at varying levels
Polished written communication: Produces clear, professional, well-organized written materials, such as status reports, proposals, and executive summaries

Skills And Attributes

Familiarity with the Project Management Institute (PMI) Guide and the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK) including understanding of the project lifecycle.
Demonstrated high-level technical understanding of business requirements as they pertain to Project Management principles and the project lifecycle including demonstrated excellent analytical and problem solving skills.
Ability to manage small, less complex work efforts, demonstrated ability to work effectively with minimum supervision and demonstrated ability to work with business sponsors and partners to identify and implement solutions including demonstrated ability to motivate teams to achieve defined deliverables.
Demonstrated ability to identify problems, mediate issues, develop solutions and implement a course of action.
Demonstrated success at meeting budget, timelines, and requirement targets and managing variances.
Demonstrated experience with Microsoft Office suite of tools and automated project management software.
Demonstrated strong interpersonal and communication skills including writing, presenting, listening, and facilitating and including demonstrated experience presenting to work effort participants, stakeholders and all levels of management.
Ability to identify milestones/deliverable delays and critical resource allocation issues from the work breakdown schedule.
Demonstrated understanding of agile delivery methodologies
Ability to manage work efforts of medium size and moderate complexity.
Demonstrated functional competencies including: Budgeting, Change Management, Client Management, Methodology Approach and Business Life Cycle, Mission/Vision/Strategy, Planning and Organization, Risk Management, Agile delivery methodologies.
Demonstrated ability to manage large scale, highly complex work efforts successfully and within budgetary guidelines.
Demonstrated strong leadership skills including ability to influence without authority
Demonstrated applied success in leading multi-disciplinary, high-performance work teams.
Demonstrated success at mentoring and developing project management skills in more junior project managers.
Experience with AI tools and technologies to enhance productivity and decision-making in professional settings highly desired

What You Will Do At Cambia

Lead estimation, planning, scope management, resource allocation, risk mitigation, and stakeholder communication to ensure successful work effort outcomes
Track and report on tasks, deliverables, costs, resources, issues, and risks; define and analyze metrics to ensure work efforts stay on target and present status to leadership and stakeholders
Create and manage comprehensive project documentation libraries, including schedules, budgets, quality plans, and communications in compliance with established standards
Oversee multiple work efforts simultaneously, ensuring timely delivery within budget while proactively recommending cost-effective solutions
Assemble project teams, assign responsibilities, identify resources, and provide guidance and direction to team members
Contribute to and ensure adherence to company-adopted project management methodologies while staying current on new approaches and generally accepted standards
May serve as ScrumMaster for one or more Agile teams, participating as a key member in agile delivery
May manage key vendor relationships and ensure timely resolution of problems within assignment scope

Pay ranges vary based on the candidate's work location. The expected hiring range depends on skills, experience, education, and training; relevant licensure / certifications; and performance history.

National pay structure — applies to the Boise and Lewiston, ID; Salt Lake City, UT, Oregon and Washington. The full salary range is $105,000 - $172,000 and the bonus target is 10%. The expected salary range is $112,000 - $151,000/year.
Regional pay structure — applies to North Dakota and Idaho and Utah locations outside the metro areas listed above: The full salary range is $95,000 - $155,000 and the bonus target is 10%. The expected salary range is $100,000 - $136,000/year.

About Cambia

Working at Cambia means being part of a purpose-driven, award-winning culture built on trust and innovation anchored in our 100+ year history. Our caring and supportive colleagues are some of the best and brightest in the industry, innovating together toward sustainable, person-focused health care. Whether we're helping members, lending a hand to a colleague or volunteering in our communities, our compassion, empathy and team spirit always shine through.

Why Join the Cambia Team?

At Cambia, You Can

Work alongside diverse teams building cutting-edge solutions to transform health care.
Earn a competitive salary and enjoy generous benefits while doing work that changes lives.
Grow your career with a company committed to helping you succeed.
Give back to your community by participating in Cambia-supported outreach programs.
Connect with colleagues who share similar interests and backgrounds through our employee resource groups.

We believe a career at Cambia is more than just a paycheck – and your compensation should be too. Our compensation package includes competitive base pay as well as a market-leading 401(k) with a significant company match, bonus opportunities and more.

Benefits

In exchange for helping members live healthy lives, we offer benefits that empower you to do the same. Just a few highlights include:

Medical, dental and vision coverage for employees and their eligible family members, including mental health benefits.
Annual employer contribution to a health savings account.
Generous paid time off varying by role and tenure in addition to 10 company-paid holidays.
Market-leading retirement plan including a company match on employee 401(k) contributions, with a potential discretionary contribution based on company performance (no vesting period).
Up to 12 weeks of paid parental time off (eligibility requires 12 months of continuous service with Cambia immediately preceding leave).
Award-winning wellness programs that reward you for participation.
Employee Assistance Fund for those in need.
Commute and parking benefits.

Learn More About Our Benefits.

We are happy to offer work from home options for most of our roles. To take advantage of this flexible option, we require employees to have a wired internet connection that is not satellite or cellular and internet service with a minimum upload speed of 5Mb and a minimum download speed of 10 Mb.

As part of our security requirements, new hires will need access to a personal mobile device to set up Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) upon joining the company. MFA is an important layer of protection for accessing Cambia systems and is required for all employees.

We are an Equal Opportunity employer dedicated to a drug and tobacco-free workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status or any other status protected by law. A background check is required.

This position serves as a Senior Capital Project Manager to provide project management services to campus partners, ensuring that design and construction projects are on schedule, within budget, responsive to program needs and comply with or exceed UNC and State Construction Office standards and expectations.

The Facilities Planning & Design department is comprised of design professionals who are responsible for the planning, design and management of all capital improvement projects across the Chapel Hill campus, and master planning and the collection and organization of space data and mapping for the greater University.

The Capital Project Management team is specifically responsible for the planning and evaluation of space needs for campus partners and auxiliary groups, providing design project management services for the University’s Capital Improvement Projects, and land use planning to create a campus environment that supports the University’s mission through master planning, development plans and agreements. The department also facilitates Community Coordination where community concerns are addressed through adherence to all zoning regulations, permit requirements and development agreements.

Requirements

Works with contracted designers, campus partners, committees, authorities, contractors, and others to assure that projects are accomplished in accordance with established guidelines, master plans, policies, and procedures. jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

Waymo's Commercialization & Strategic PMO Technical Program Managers are accountable for delivering Waymo's commercial business lines, platform expansion, and strategic new initiatives. We provide thoughtful cross-functional planning, clarity, and proactive risk management. When a new product has no established playbook, we act with thoughtful urgency to structure the work, drive decisions, and align teams across organizations. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Hardware, Safety, Legal, and Operations to take new initiatives from early concept to real-world launch.

This role follows a hybrid work schedule, and you will report to the Director of Technical Program Management, Commercialization & Strategic PMO.

You Will

Architect and lead the holistic, cross-organizational technical program for Waymo's New Product Programs initiatives
Own and drive the end-to-end program structure, work breakdown, and master schedule across pillars, delegating sub-projects across domain TPMs while retaining accountability for the holistic program and its interdependencies.
Serve as a strategic technical partner to Product and Engineering leadership across TaaS, Fleet & Operations, Onboard Autonomy, Hardware, and Systems/Safety Engineering
Simplify interfaces across organizational boundaries by establishing scalable operating frameworks, cross-org structures, and readiness playbooks.
Occasional travel between Bay Area offices, test facilities/depots, OEM partner sites, or expansion markets, about one week per quarter (~10%).

You Have

10+ years of experience leading transformational, multi-organization technical programs from 0-to-1 conception through public launch and scaled operations across hardware, embedded/onboard software, cloud/mobile platforms, and physical operations.
Demonstrated technical judgment equivalent to a senior/staff practicing engineer (L5+ SWE): ability to influence strategic technical direction, evaluate complex system architectures across onboard and offboard stacks, and broker high-stakes velocity vs. quality decisions.
A proven track record of structuring ambiguous, company-level initiatives into unambiguous work breakdowns, milestones, and accountability frameworks while managing a portfolio of interdependent workstreams and guiding other TPMs.
Deep experience in resource management, capacity forecasting, and financial/unit-economics modeling across large distributed engineering organizations (100+ engineers) without direct line authority.
Experience navigating safety-critical, regulated, or hardware-software integrated consumer products where product readiness, verification & validation (V&V), and field operations must converge on strict release cadences.
Exceptional executive presence and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to influence VP/C-level leadership, align multidisciplinary leads (Engineering, Product, Legal, Safety, Operations, OEM Partnerships), and drive organizational change.

We Prefer

Experience in autonomous vehicles, automotive OEM platform programs, robotics, aerospace, or complex consumer hardware-software ecosystems with long hardware freeze lead times.
A track record of taking a net-new business line or incubation program inside a scaled technology company from early prototype/fishfood to external customer pilot and commercial agreement.
Familiarity with automotive regulatory and homologation frameworks (DMV, CPUC, NHTSA, FMVSS, multi-stage manufacturing), consumer auto insurance/underwriting, or physical fleet/depot operations.
Experience mentoring, coordinating, and scaling a cohort of Technical Program Managers across multiple functional pillars (e.g., Onboard, Cloud/Mobile, Fleet, Release/Safety).

We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Hardware, Safety, Legal, and Operations to take new initiatives from early concept to real-world launch.

This role follows a hybrid work schedule, and you will report to the Director of Technical Program Management, Commercialization & Strategic PMO.

You Will

Architect and lead the holistic, cross-organizational technical program for Waymo's New Product Programs initiatives
Own and drive the end-to-end program structure, work breakdown, and master schedule across pillars, delegating sub-projects across domain TPMs while retaining accountability for the holistic program and its interdependencies.
Serve as a strategic technical partner to Product and Engineering leadership across TaaS, Fleet & Operations, Onboard Autonomy, Hardware, and Systems/Safety Engineering
Simplify interfaces across organizational boundaries by establishing scalable operating frameworks, cross-org structures, and readiness playbooks.
Occasional travel between Bay Area offices, test facilities/depots, OEM partner sites, or expansion markets, about one week per quarter (~10%).

You Have

10+ years of experience leading transformational, multi-organization technical programs from 0-to-1 conception through public launch and scaled operations across hardware, embedded/onboard software, cloud/mobile platforms, and physical operations.
Demonstrated technical judgment equivalent to a senior/staff practicing engineer (L5+ SWE): ability to influence strategic technical direction, evaluate complex system architectures across onboard and offboard stacks, and broker high-stakes velocity vs. quality decisions.
A proven track record of structuring ambiguous, company-level initiatives into unambiguous work breakdowns, milestones, and accountability frameworks while managing a portfolio of interdependent workstreams and guiding other TPMs.
Deep experience in resource management, capacity forecasting, and financial/unit-economics modeling across large distributed engineering organizations (100+ engineers) without direct line authority.
Experience navigating safety-critical, regulated, or hardware-software integrated consumer products where product readiness, verification & validation (V&V), and field operations must converge on strict release cadences.
Exceptional executive presence and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to influence VP/C-level leadership, align multidisciplinary leads (Engineering, Product, Legal, Safety, Operations, OEM Partnerships), and drive organizational change.

We Prefer

Experience in autonomous vehicles, automotive OEM platform programs, robotics, aerospace, or complex consumer hardware-software ecosystems with long hardware freeze lead times.
A track record of taking a net-new business line or incubation program inside a scaled technology company from early prototype/fishfood to external customer pilot and commercial agreement.
Familiarity with automotive regulatory and homologation frameworks (DMV, CPUC, NHTSA, FMVSS, multi-stage manufacturing), consumer auto insurance/underwriting, or physical fleet/depot operations.
Experience mentoring, coordinating, and scaling a cohort of Technical Program Managers across multiple functional pillars (e.g., Onboard, Cloud/Mobile, Fleet, Release/Safety).

jobs.description:
At ABB, we help industries outrun - leaner and cleaner. Here, progress is an expectation - for you, your team, and the world. As a global market leader, we’ll give you what you need to make it happen. It won’t always be easy, growing takes grit. But at ABB, you’ll never run alone. Run what runs the world.

This role sits within ABB's Robotics business, a leading global robotics company. We're entering an exciting new chapter as we’ve announced the plan for SoftBank Group to acquire ABB Robotics. SoftBank is a globally recognized technology group and investor/operator focused on AI, robotics, and next-generation computing. By joining us now, you’ll be part of a pioneering team shaping the future of robotics—working alongside world-class experts in a fast-moving, innovation-driven environment.

This Position Reports To

Business Process Manager

We Are Hiring 3 Implementation Managers To Drive Our Global Quote-to-Order Transformation. You Will Join a Key Initiative To Standardize Commercial Processes And Digital Solutions Across Our Business. Apply For The Region That Matches Your Profile And Career Aspirations

Europe — Flexible location across European countries
America — Flexible location across American countries

Each role is autonomous and high-impact, with direct influence on how our commercial operations work in your region.

About The Role

Join ABB Robotics as an Implementation Manager and drive the implementation and adoption of our global Quote-to-Order process and supporting digital solutions.

The role will work closely with country commercial organizations to understand their current ways of working, introduce the global Quote-to-Order process, identify gaps and local requirements, and support countries through the transition to the target process and tools. The current solution landscape includes CPQ and the commercial Quote-to-Order processes interfacing with SAP S/4HANA
, together with other supporting applications. The scope may evolve as the Quote-to-Order process and application landscape develops. The position is part of the Commercial Excellence – Quote to Order Process
organization and reports to the Quote to Order Process Manager
.

This is a high-impact, cross-functional role at the heart of our commercial transformation.

What You Will Do

Lead implementation of the global Quote-to-Order process across your region.
Facilitate workshops to map current country processes against the global target, identify gaps, and define how they are resolved.
Support countries through a complete tool landscape transformation — you'll be equally comfortable helping teams understand new processes and navigating new tools.
Act as the primary business process advisor and second-level tool support contact for your region's countries — balancing process discipline with pragmatic tool troubleshooting
Coordinate deployment of CPQ and related solutions, including the commercial process integration and handover into SAP S/4HANA.
Act as the primary Quote-to-Order implementation contact for your region’s countries, building trusted relationships with sales organizations and key stakeholders.
Build strong relationships with country Sales organizations and key stakeholders. Understand existing country commercial processes, requirements and ways of working and support countries through the change management process.
Define and execute country implementation plans covering preparation, testing, training, go-live and stabilization. Coordinate user acceptance testing and implementation readiness with countries and IT/IS teams.
Champion continuous improvement post go-live, translating recurring business challenges into structured requirements for process and tool enhancements.

What You Bring

3-5 years of proven experience in commercial process implementation, digital transformation or business change roles in a B2B environment.
Good understanding of commercial processes such as quotation, pricing, configuration, sales operations or order handling.
Experience working with commercial platforms such as CPQ, CRM, CLM or ERP is an advantage.
Experience with commercial processes integrated with SAP S/4HANA or comparable ERP environments is an advantage.
Strong stakeholder management and facilitation skills. You are equally confident with business and technical audiences.
Experience working across multiple countries and in matrix organizations; structured, self-driven and ownership-oriented.
Fluent in English; local or regional language skills are an advantage. Willingness to travel frequently within your region, particularly during implementation phases.

The Ideal Candidate

You combine commercial understanding, process orientation and change management expertise. You know how to sit with a country team, understand how they work today, and guide them confidently toward a standardized global process, without losing sight of legitimate local needs. You do not need to be a Process Owner, CPQ specialist or ERP expert, but you must have enough breadth across commercial, process and systems topics to lead implementation to successful adoption.

About Johnson Controls

Johnson Controls, a global leader in thermal management, mission-critical building systems, energy efficiency, and decarbonization, helps customers use energy more productively, reduce carbon emissions, and operate with the precision and resilience required in rapidly expanding industries such as data centers, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, advanced manufacturing, and higher education.

For more than 140 years, Johnson Controls has delivered performance where it really matters. Backed by advanced technology, lifecycle services and an industry-leading field organization, we elevate customer performance, turn goals into real-world results and help move society forward.

What we offer

Competitive salary. 
Paid vacation/holidays/sick time. 
Company vehicle, depending on work location.
Comprehensive benefits package including, medical, dental, and vision care
Extensive product and on the job/cross training opportunities, with outstanding resources. 
Encouraging and collaborative team environment. 
Dedication to safety through our Zero Harm policy.

What Will You Do

The National Project Manager is an integral part of our national operations group, and acts as project leader to plan, execute, and complete access control, CCTV, intrusion alarm and intercom system projects with assigned national customers. Works with appropriate technical team to ensure National Program Standards are updated and distributed as necessary per account. Acts as a single point-of-contact on JCI’s behalf for large national accounts. Works closely with local branch level operations (ISTM/IC/SC) to ensure success in install and service performance for national accounts.

The National Project Manager will also be responsible for overseeing the service program for specific accounts, as well as maintaining visibility and tracking of all project updates, submittals, deliverables, invoicing and escalations for same. Responsible to actively pursues change orders, and maintain effective and timely communication with the assigned National Project Team within JCI for the assigned accounts.

The National Project Manager maintains an effective balance between customer satisfaction and project financial results, coordinates communication with the customer during all phases of the project. Provides work direction to subcontractors, installers, technicians, designers, and administration as necessary. Ensures work performed is in compliance with required applicable codes and standards and operates on the job with the highest of ethics.

How Will You Do It

Oversee project lifecycle from start to finish through various stages – Booking, kick-off, scheduling, mobilization, RFI/change orders, job completion, close out, and invoicing. Provides detailed information to communicate design and operation to customers, Johnson Controls staff and subcontractors.
Actively pursues additional work through change orders when justified. Evaluates the contractual scope of work and the impact of client issued bulletins, field directives and/or scheduling changes. Communicates both technical and business-related issues with the clients.
Oversee effective and timely ordering and receipt of job materials and subsequent scheduling of projects within defined project requirements.
Through close communication with local branches, provides jobsite coordination based on developed Scope of Work and National Program Standards details. Ensures installation is in accordance with Johnson Controls literature and project requirements.
Ensure projects are completed within time, budget and scope. Validates complete system functionality based on available criteria-of-completion and resolves issues to ensure proper operation. Compiles and provides accurate project as-built and commissioning documentation where required.
Oversee the overall cost, billings and collections for assigned accounts. Works closely with billing/invoicing team to ensure invoices are submitted timely after project is considered completed and accepted by customer. Maintains profitability goals and positive cash flow.
Provides coaching, mentoring and technical assistance to field technicians. Provides technical assistance to subcontractors. Ensures that delegated tasks are done accurately, on-time, billed, within budget and within scope of the contract.
Effectively communicates the status of projects to management as required.
Maintain detailed and up-to-date tracking of all projects, including milestone tracking, material receipt, on-site tech scheduling, forecasted completion dates, individual project escalations and/or challenges, and invoicing.
Where applicable, sends warranty letter to JCI customer upon substantial completion of project and ensures proper execution of warranty.
Develops project plans and coordinates the required resources to ensure timely and cost-effective installation and completion of assigned projects.
Coordinates site-specific training for owner/operator on the total system in full or with assistance. Ensures owner/operator has been trained. Provides proper documentation and manuals for system operation.
Develops and maintains viable long-term relationships with contractors, clients, consultants and subcontractors. Attends job progress meetings as required.
Adheres to safety standards. High degree of regard to employee and subcontractor safety.

Required

What we look for

 4 years minimum prior experience with project or program management, or technical management role or 8 years minimum field tech experience in Fire & Security industry dealing with large complex projects.
Must have working knowledge of electricity and electronics. Specific technical knowledge of electronic security and IT network systems is strongly recommended due to the technical aspect of this position.
Must have the ability to communicate technical material to a non-technical audience.
Ability to effectively work independently.
Demonstrate a high level of customer service.
Strong working capabilities in MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Project), Adobe Writer, Visio and basic Windows environment.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to read and understand complex building architectural, mechanical and electrical documents, as well as project plans, specifications, schedules and equipment installation/operation/troubleshooting manual.

Preferred

Has PMI/PMP or CSPM accreditation, or willing to obtain within 2 years of employment in the position.
Experience in dealing with a large and diverse number of simultaneous challenges, requiring knowledge of many different disciplines.
Has or is currently eligible for government security clearance within Canada (Reliability, Secret, or Top Secret) due to the restricted nature of many National Accounts.
Knowledge of applicable industry and national standards – Various CAN/ULC standards related to security installation and monitoring, OBC/NBC building standards, fire code.

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Space Systems designs, builds and delivers space, defense and aviation-related systems to customers around the world. Our main products include launch vehicles and related propulsion systems; missile products, subsystems and defense electronics; precision weapons, armament systems and ammunition; satellites and associated space components and services; and advanced aerospace structures.

Northrop Grumman is currently seeking a Program Manager 2
for the Hypersonic - Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) Program in our Propulsion Systems Business Unit at Promontory, Utah.

This position is 100% on-site.

The Program Manager will support program implementation and execution. Emphasis is in communication with external and internal customers and functional organizations, and overall management of group financial and contract commitments. The position is located at Promontory as part of the Missiles Program Operating Unit. Overall, the Program Manager will be responsible for executing existing programs and developing and executing business growth strategies. The Program Manager must also be able to travel to all three campuses i.e. Bacchus, Clearfield, and Promontory, Utah.

Lead program execution across safety, quality, schedule, technology, and cost.
Apply knowledge of energetic materials, solid rocket motors, and related components.
Drive results, challenge the status quo, and promote continuous improvement.
Mentor team members and influence stakeholders effectively.
Represent Northrop Grumman to customers and align company capabilities with customer needs.
Resolve customer and program issues in accordance with business objectives, contracts, regulations, and company requirements.
Balance the interests of customers, the company, and employees.
Lead program participation in customer working groups.
Provide leadership, direction, coaching, and conflict resolution for cross-functional program teams.
Establish and communicate program priorities.
Communicate clearly, concisely, and persuasively in both written and verbal formats.
Manage contract baseline changes, program risks, corrective actions, and master plans.
Maintain alignment with program milestones, integrated master schedules, factory schedules, and Earned Value Management requirements.
Oversee program budgets, financial forecasts, and monthly business reviews.
Align program activities and communications to maximize award-fee performance.
Support contract negotiations, pricing, contract changes, terms, and issue resolution.
Drive technical excellence by establishing standards, managing risk, and ensuring delivery of required performance.
Identify and pursue new business opportunities through existing programs.
Lead the preparation of new, follow-on, and change proposals in alignment with company strategy and customer requirements.
Travel approximately 25% of the time.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or Business discipline with 10 years’ related experience; or 8 years with a Master’s degree
5 plus years’ experience leading cross functional teams
Experience in aerospace manufacturing
Ability to deliver results to the bottom line and managing change
Experience in cost and schedule controls, including IMS management
Proven experience in profit & loss accountability
Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret Clearance

Working knowledge of solid rocket design, motor development and production
Familiar with Promontory and Nozzle Value Streams
Understanding of Earned Value Management System
Experience in integration of the VSET concept with PS program execution and VSET management
Experience supporting US Government contracts
Familiarity and experience in managing CUI data

Primary Level Salary Range: $139,100.00 - $208,700.00

Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is seeking an Environmental Permitting Project Manage
r to support our Permitting, Planning, and Licensing practice in North Florida (located either in Gainesville
or Jacksonville
) .
This role will focus on managing the permitting strategy, environmental compliance, natural resource assessments, and regulatory coordination for a variety of projects within the energy, oil & gas, utilities, transportation, industrial, government, and infrastructure sectors.

The selected candidate will manage permitting and environmental planning projects, working closely with subject matter experts, biologists, environmental planners, engineers, and regulatory specialists. Responsibilities will include developing permitting strategies, preparing regulatory documentation, supporting business development efforts, managing project tasks, and mentoring junior staff. Projects may involve federal, state, and local permitting, natural resource assessments, wetland and waters evaluations, threatened and endangered species coordination, mitigation planning, and environmental compliance support throughout project lifecycles.

We are seeking a candidate who brings strong technical expertise, regulatory knowledge, project management capabilities, and a solution-oriented mindset to help deliver successful projects while contributing to the continued growth of WSP's practice throughout Florida and the southeast.

Your Impact

Support and lead environmental permitting and natural resource projects throughout Florida and the southeast.
Develop permitting strategies and regulatory pathways for infrastructure, energy, utility, transportation, industrial, and infrastructure projects.
Prepare and review permit applications, technical reports, environmental assessments, and supporting documentation.
Contribute to staffing plans and manage multidisciplinary teams, teaming partners, and subcontractors to meet project requirements and client commitments.
Coordinate with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies to facilitate project approvals.
Plan, coordinate, and provide technical oversight for wetland delineations, habitat assessments, threatened and endangered species evaluations, and other natural resource studies.
Provide clients with environmental compliance and permitting guidance throughout project development and implementation.
Develop project scopes, schedules, budgets, and proposals.
Manage multiple projects while ensuring quality deliverables are completed on time and within budget.
Analyze and interpret environmental data and provide technical review and quality assurance.
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to support environmental reviews, permit applications, mitigation plans, and resource management strategies.
Mentor and support the professional development of junior environmental staff.
Build and maintain strong client relationships and support business development initiatives; help convert successful project delivery into repeat business.
Foster a culture of technical excellence, collaboration, innovation, and exceptional client service.
Promote a strong safety culture and maintain compliance with WSP health and safety standards.
Exercise sound and ethical decision-making in accordance with WSP policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.
Manage project financial performance, including forecasting, invoicing, change management, risk identification and corrective actions needed to achieve scope, schedule, budget, quality and profitability goals.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in biology, environmental science, natural resources, environmental planning, ecology, geography, or a related field.
Minimum of 7 years of experience in natural resources, environmental permitting, environmental consulting, or a related field.
Experience supporting projects in Florida and the southeast.
Strong understanding of environmental permitting processes and regulatory frameworks, including NEPA, Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, Endangered Species Act, and related state regulations.
Experience coordinating with agencies such as USACE, USFWS, NOAA, EPA, and Florida and other state regulatory agencies.
Knowledge of wetland permitting, habitat assessments, ecological surveys, mitigation planning, and environmental compliance requirements.
Demonstrated project management experience, including scope development, budget management, and client communication.
Strong technical writing and communication skills with experience preparing reports, permit applications, and presentations.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary consulting environment.
Proven commitment to workplace safety and quality project delivery.
Ability to travel, including occasional overnight travel for client meetings, agency coordination, and project initiation.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in environmental science, biology, ecology, natural resource management, environmental planning, or related field.
Previous project management experience in the environmental field.
Experience managing multidisciplinary environmental and permitting projects.
Experience with large-scale energy, utility, transportation, coastal restoration, or infrastructure projects.
Established relationships with regulatory agencies and clients throughout Florida and the southeast.
Experience mentoring and developing junior staff.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or similar credential.
Professional Wetland Scientist

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

www.wsp.com

At WSP, we want to give our employees the challenges they seek to grow their careers and knowledge base. Your daily contributions to your team will be essential in meeting client objectives, goals and challenges. Are you ready to get started?

Northrop Grumman Defense Systems Sector is currently seeking a Munitions Program Manager 2
, in our growing Fuzing and Warhead business, within our Missile Products Business Unit (BU), at our Plymouth, MN location.

In this role, the selected leader will be responsible for delivery of all contractual requirements on cost and on schedule, while achieving all technical requirements and creating customer intimacy to develop further opportunities. The individual will lead a cross-functional organization aligned to common program performance goals. This position will support various programs within the business unit portfolio of programs and will report directly to the Program Director.

Responsibilities

Program Managers are responsible for leading all phases of the program life cycle from inception (proposal development) through startup, execution, and completion (contract closeout). Primary responsibilities are the management of cost, schedule, and technical performance of company programs or subsystems and include, but are not limited to:

Cultivating and maintaining effective customer relationships and intimacy to develop further opportunities within the customer community

Ensuring adherence to all internal processes, policies, and applicable industry standards

Developing, managing adherence to master program plans and schedules
Developing, managing and conducting thorough risk & opportunity management practices including identification, mitigation and realization

Desired Attributes

Excellent interpersonal skills with ability to manage a project team daily and communicate effectively with segment leadership regarding status, awareness, and escalations
Ability to resolve disputes and negotiate with positive outcome while maintaining good relationships within the organization, specifically between peers and management
Ability to manage projects to specified milestones and established schedules
Ability to manage communications with stakeholders through organized processes to ensure that program information is defined, collected, shared, understood, stored and retrieved in a manner that effectively meets program and stakeholder needs
Ability to identify and address program impacts through a systematic, proactive approach to issue and problem resolution that identifies, communicates, monitors, and promptly resolves conflicts across all levels of the program
Ability to define proposal strategy, lead proposal teams, analyze and shape RFPs, produce and deliver winning proposals, effectively track and incorporate Review Team comments and findings, and manage post-proposal submittals (orals, finding responses)
Ability to address program uncertainty through an organized and analytical forward-looking approach that identifies risks and opportunities, determines appropriate handling plans, and manages, controls, and communicates risks and opportunities throughout the lifecycle of the program

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree and 8 years of experience OR a Master’s degree and 6 years of experience supporting U.S. Government contracts and customers and project management in other industries
8 years of experience leading the performance of tasks on schedule, at cost and achieving all requirements as either a project lead, integrated program team lead or cost account manager
6 years of demonstrated success leading teams/and or organizations to achieve a common goal
Competency in Project Management skills and toolsets
Knowledge of pricing and proposals
Competent in standard Microsoft Office Suite (i.e. PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Outlook)
Ability to obtain and maintain a US Government DoW Secret clearance

Preferred Qualifications

A degree in a science, engineering, or a business program
Experience in the aerospace/defense industry or within the Department of Defense or NASA
PMP® certification
Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, Agile methodologies
Ability to define technical strategy to promote capturing business in new areas
Current US Government DoW Secret clearance

.

Lead implementation of the global Quote-to-Order process across your region.
Facilitate workshops to map current country processes against the global target, identify gaps, and define how they are resolved.
Support countries through a complete tool landscape transformation — you'll be equally comfortable helping teams understand new processes and navigating new tools.

Coordinate deployment of CPQ and related solutions, including the commercial process integration and handover into SAP S/4HANA.

What You Bring

3-5 years of proven experience in commercial process implementation, digital transformation or business change roles in a B2B environment.

You do not need to be a Process Owner, CPQ specialist or ERP expert, but you must have enough breadth across commercial, process and systems topics to lead implementation to successful adoption.

Knowledge of SAP logistics modules, including Warehouse Management, Logistics Execution and Materials Management.

jobs.title: Litigation Research Analyst
jobs.description:
Overview

Analysis Group is one of the largest international economics consulting firms, with more than 1,500 professionals across 15 offices in North America, Europe, and Asia. Since 1981, we have provided expertise in economics, finance, health care analytics, and strategy to top law firms, Fortune Global 500 companies, and government agencies worldwide. Our internal experts, together with our network of affiliated experts from academia, industry, and government, offer our clients exceptional breadth and depth of expertise.

The Research & Knowledge Services (RKS) team partners with case teams, business functions, and firm leadership to generate intelligence that supports litigation-related research, competitive analysis, and market insights. The team sits within the Marketing & Business Development (MBD) department and collaborates closely with colleagues across the firm.

Our team is looking for a highly motivated research professional with strong analytical instincts, a command of legal and business databases, and the ability to synthesize complex information into clear, actionable outputs. The Litigation Research Analyst will conduct a wide range of research requests — spanning expert witness materials, court filings, legal trends, and competitor intelligence — on behalf of individual consultants, practice groups, and the firm. They will actively contribute to the internal systems and workflows that make research outputs reusable and accessible over time. The role requires intellectual curiosity, creativity and enjoyment in solving intricate research questions, exceptional attention to detail and accuracy, and strong judgment in assessing the relevance and credibility of research results.

Essential Job Functions And Responsibilities

Expert Witness Research and Legal Research Support
Evaluate incoming research requests to clarify scope, objectives, and expected deliverables.
Conduct legal, litigation, and business development research using internal and external tools, including CourtLink, Bloomberg Law, LexisNexis, Westlaw, CRM systems, SharePoint, expert materials repositories, and other knowledge management resources.
Locate, review, and summarize publicly available expert witness materials and litigation documents, including reports, testimony, motions, and related filings.
Prepare clear, concise research outputs, including litigation histories, matter summaries, legal trends summaries, and competitor insights.
Identify opportunities to leverage expert materials and related research assets for business development, competitive intelligence, practice development, litigation trend analysis, and knowledge sharing.

Workflow and Systems Improvements
Help evaluate and refine workflows for locating, reviewing, storing, annotating, and reusing expert materials and related litigation documents.
Maintain and improve databases, trackers, CRM records, and other internal systems to support information organization, data quality, retrieval, and reuse.
Identify and prototype AI-enabled efficiencies in document review, summarization, tagging, annotation, structured information extraction, and knowledge retrieval workflows.

Collaboration and Ownership
Collaborate with colleagues across RKS, Marketing & Business Development, practice groups, and other firm functions on research projects, business development efforts, knowledge management priorities, and other marketing-related initiatives.Take ownership of assigned expert research, document retrieval, repository maintenance, and recurring service responsibilities.
Proactively surface questions, gaps, and opportunities to improve the usefulness, reliability, and accessibility of RKS outputs.
Over time, develop a proactive role in shaping expert research best practices, identifying emerging needs, and recommending ways to leverage and improve existing resources.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required.
Minimum of 3 years of substantive relevant experience required.
An ideal candidate will have 4 to 6 years of professional experience in legal research, litigation support, law firm library or research services, or a related environment.
Strong familiarity with legal research, litigation dockets, and court filings required.
Experience with legal research platforms such as CourtLink, Bloomberg Law, LexisNexis, Westlaw, Lex Machina, Law360, or similar resources required.
Demonstrated intellectual curiosity, persistence, and creativity in locating difficult-to-find information, including the ability to adapt research strategies when standard sources or processes do not produce complete results.
Comfort working on research questions that may not have a clear step-by-step path, including the ability to identify leads, test alternative sources, and evaluate relevance.
Strong judgment, analytical reasoning, problem-solving ability, and attention to detail.
Proven ability to organize, plan, and manage multiple projects simultaneously while remaining flexible in response to shifting priorities and deadlines.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to summarize legal and expert-related research findings clearly for different audiences.
Self-motivated, collaborative, and eager to learn, contribute, and take ownership of assignments.
Interest in Generative AI tools or large language model-based workflows for document review or information extraction is a plus.
Experience with CRM or knowledge management systems preferred.
An inclusive and growth-oriented mindset, strong interpersonal skills, and an ability to work across functions.
To the extent permitted by applicable law, eligible candidates must be authorized to work in the United States, without sponsorship or restriction, now and in the future.

jobs.description:
Explore opportunities with the Enterprise Information Security (EIS) team at UnitedHealth Group
. Join one of the world's largest health care companies and become part of the first line of defense against security threats. We are focused on strengthening our cyber defenses, ransomware resiliency, vulnerability mitigation, and securing all aspects of our systems and data globally. We are passionate about protecting the sensitive data of our members and providers. We are committed to leveraging every tool, partnership and process needed to enhance our security posture. It is our duty to protect the information of those we serve while  Caring. Connecting. Growing together.

The Enterprise Information Security (EIS) team
 is responsible for cybersecurity across our organization. We support our business and members by reducing risk, rapidly responding to threats, focusing on business resiliency and securing new acquisitions.

As a Principal Cybersecurity Analyst on the Attack Surface Management (ASM) team within Optum Technology's Enterprise Information Security organization, you will provide senior technical leadership to protect our global enterprise against emerging digital threats. In this role, you will lead the identification, mapping, assessment, and exposure management of external and internal digital assets across complex multi-cloud and on-premises environments. You will partner across cyber defense, threat intelligence, vulnerability management, and engineering teams to illuminate security blind spots, evaluate risk vectors, and design automated reconnaissance and remediation workflows. By integrating modern, enterprise-approved AI tools and intelligent automation into daily operations, you will drive operational efficiency and elevate the proactive cyber resilience of healthcare platforms trusted by millions.

You'll enjoy the flexibility to work remotely * from anywhere within the U.S. as you take on some tough challenges. For all hires in the Minneapolis or Washington, D.C. area, you will be required to work in the office a minimum of four days per week.

Primary Responsibilities

Lead the strategic expansion and daily execution of the enterprise Attack Surface Management (ASM) program, establishing comprehensive visibility of external and internal digital assets across multi-cloud and on-premises environments
Perform continuous discovery, validation, and risk analysis of public-facing infrastructure, cloud environments, domains, APIs, and third-party dependencies to pinpoint vulnerabilities and misconfigurations
Partner closely with Threat Intelligence, Vulnerability Management, and Red Team operations to correlate exposure data with active threats and prioritize remediation efforts
Design, build, and deploy automated discovery, scanning, and notification pipelines to accelerate time-to-detection and exposure remediation
Use enterprise-approved AI tools to streamline workflows, automate tasks, and drive continuous improvement across vulnerability assessment and attack surface analysis
Evaluate emerging trends to inform solution design, security architecture, and strategic innovation across attack surface management
Collaborate with cloud engineering, DevOps, and IT application owners to ensure proactive remediation and embed security controls into continuous deployment pipelines
Perform QA/QC of team member tickets and tasks to ensure operational quality, while mentoring and guiding junior and mid-level analysts
Identify and implement continuous process and cross-functional collaboration improvements
Maintain the team documentation library, standard operating procedures, and technical playbooks
Enhance vendor relationships and support to optimize tooling effectiveness and service delivery

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of experience in cybersecurity, information security, or security operations
5+ years of dedicated experience in attack surface management (ASM), external exposure monitoring, vulnerability assessment, or threat intelligence
3+ years of experience assessing asset configurations and security postures across major public cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP)
3+ years of hands-on experience utilizing enterprise ASM, threat exposure, or vulnerability discovery platforms (e.g., Cortex Xpanse, Censys, Tenable, Qualys, or Shodan
Experience in cyber threat intelligence and/or an investigatory role
Proven solid communication and writing abilities (technical, analytical, and business)
Available to support daily operations as well as (on an ad-hoc basis) off-hour war room efforts

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)
Experience developing scripts (e.g., Python, Bash, or PowerShell) and leveraging REST APIs for automated data collection, alerting, and workflow integration
Industry-recognized cybersecurity certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CEH, OSCP, or GIAC certifications such as GCIH, GPEN)
Cloud security certifications (e.g., AWS Certified Security - Specialty, Microsoft Certified: Azure Security Engineer Associate)
Experience leveraging approved AI productivity and data analysis tools to augment security evaluations, synthesize threat data, or automate routine tasks
Solid understanding of cybersecurity frameworks and taxonomies (e.g., MITRE ATT&CK, NIST CSF, OWASP Top 10, CIS Critical Security Controls)
Experience operating within large-scale, distributed enterprise environments subject to healthcare regulations (e.g., HIPAA, HITRUST) or financial industry standards

jobs.description:
Requirements

Description & Requirements

who we are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. Setting the bar in technical fabrics and functional design, we create transformational products and experiences that support people in moving, growing, connecting, and being well. We owe our success to our innovative product, emphasis on stores, commitment to our people, and the incredible connections we make in every community we're in. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

About This Team

The lululemon cybersecurity team enables lululemon to conduct its global operations in a secure manner and safeguard the trusted information of its guest and users. This is accomplished by understanding business risk as manifested through cybersecurity and compliance risk, and by maintain a high degree of employee awareness of all security and compliance topics. To further enhance our team, we are looking for an experienced Cyber Security Senior Analyst.

A Day In The Life

The Cyber Security Senior Analyst will help the team to perform Security Operations Center (SOC) duties, which include incident response, malware analysis, and monitoring. This role will work with the team and become a senior technical contributor to implement and apply technologies, processes, and practices designed to protect networks, devices, and data from malicious attack, damage, or unauthorized access.

Conduct threat analysis, assessment, and malware analysis in support of security investigations and incident response processes.
Lead investigations into security incidents escalated from lower-tier SOC analysts.
Provide technical mentorship to Tier 1 and Tier 2 SOC analysts, sharing knowledge on incident response, threat detection, and advanced cybersecurity techniques.
Conduct root cause analysis and identify containment and remediation actions.
Recognize and research attacker tools, tactics, and procedures (TTP) in indicators of compromise (IOCs) that can be applied to current and future investigations.
Build internal scripts, tools, and automation processes to enhance detection and response capabilities.
Collaborate with technical and business teams to drive SOC initiatives acting as the SME.
Conduct threat hunting activities to proactively identify potential threats and vulnerabilities within the network.
Develop and maintain SOC runbooks and documentation to ensure consistent and effective processes.
Participate in security audits and assessments to ensure compliance with industry standards and regulations.
Provide after-hour support as needed and participate in on-call rotation.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in cybersecurity, computer science, information technology, or related field.
5+ years experience in a Security Operations Center or Technical Incident Response role.
Strong knowledge of incident response methodologies, including NIST 800-61.
Proven track record of handling advanced and complex security incidents.
Demonstrated experience in computer security-related disciplines such as incident response, host forensics, malware analysis, container security, network traffic analysis, Insider Threat, alert tuning, and trend analysis.
Strong knowledge of cloud security in Azure, AWS, GCP.
Extensive experience working with security tools such as Azure Sentinel, Splunk, Microsoft Defender Security Suite, firewalls, IDS/IPS, antispam, content management, server and network device hardening, etc.
Strong understanding of security concepts and threat categories (such as malware, phishing attacks, Defense-in-Depth, MITRE ATT&CK framework, Cyber Kill Chain, etc.).
Strong knowledge of Windows, Linux, and Mac OS
Advanced Experience with query languages such as KQL and SPL
Experience with scripting languages such as Bash, PowerShell, or Python.

jobs.title: Credit Research Analyst
jobs.description:
Your opportunity

At Schwab, you’re empowered to make an impact on your career. Here, innovative thought meets creative problem solving, helping us challenge the status quo and transform the finance industry together.

We believe in the importance of in-office collaboration and fully intend for the selected candidate for this role to work on site in the specified location(s).

As a Senior Analyst within Credit Research, you will provide independent research and recommendations on asset-backed commercial paper programs and asset-backed securities held across fixed income and money market portfolios. Your analysis will help portfolio managers and credit committees make informed investment decisions and identify emerging collateral, structural, liquidity, and counterparty risks.

You will evaluate transaction structures, collateral performance, credit enhancement, cash flow waterfalls, and liquidity support; perform modeling, stress testing, and ongoing surveillance; and translate complex findings into clear, actionable recommendations. You will own assigned coverage, prioritize time-sensitive reviews, and collaborate with portfolio management, trading, risk management, issuers, servicers, rating agencies, and other research partners.

Success requires structured finance expertise, analytical thinking, sound decision-making, clear communication, and adaptability as market conditions, portfolio needs, and research tools evolve. You will also help strengthen research methodologies, data analytics, automation, and AI-enabled surveillance capabilities.

What you have

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, accounting, business, or a related field
3+ years of experience in credit research, structured finance, fixed income analysis, banking, a rating agency, or a related investment discipline
Working knowledge of asset-backed commercial paper (ABCP) programs, including program structure, program-wide and seller-specific credit enhancement, liquidity facilities, asset eligibility and concentration criteria and seller/servicer quality
Working knowledge of asset-backed securities (ABS) across collateral types, including cash flow waterfalls, credit enhancement, collateral performance, servicer and originator quality, and review of transaction documents and trustee reports
Ability to develop well-supported credit recommendations and communicate complex findings clearly to portfolio managers, credit committees, and cross-functional partners
Strong analytical thinking, decision-making, collaboration, and adaptability when evaluating changing market conditions and emerging risks

Preferred Qualifications

Experience performing cash flow modeling, scenario analysis, or stress testing for structured finance transactions
Experience with structured finance analytics platforms or credit surveillance systems
Advanced Microsoft Excel and financial modeling capabilities
Familiarity with data analytics, automation, or AI-enabled research workflows
Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills

In addition to the salary range, this role is eligible for bonus or incentive opportunities.

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan
Paid time for vacation, volunteering, and 28-day sabbatical after every 5 years of service for eligible positions
Paid parental leave and family building benefits
Tuition reimbursement
Health, dental, and vision insurance
